@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_multipart_closes_tempfile_on_any_interruption() -> None:
    """Temporary files must be closed when the parse is interrupted by any exception."""
    closed: list[SpooledTemporaryFile[bytes]] = []

    class TrackingSpooledTemporaryFile(SpooledTemporaryFile[bytes]):
        def close(self) -> None:
            closed.append(self)
            super().close()

    boundary = "a7f7ac8d4e2e437c877bb7b8d7cc549c"
    first_chunk = (
        f"--{boundary}\r\n"
        f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="test.txt"\r\n'
        f"Content-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\n"
        f"partial content"
    ).encode()

    async def stream() -> AsyncGenerator[bytes, None]:
        yield first_chunk
        raise RuntimeError("interrupted")

    headers = Headers({"Content-Type": f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}"})
    parser = MultiPartParser(headers, stream())
    with mock.patch("starlette.formparsers.SpooledTemporaryFile", TrackingSpooledTemporaryFile):
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="interrupted"):
            await parser.parse()

    assert len(closed) == 1
EOF

structured_output.summary:
Added RequestBodyLimitMiddleware (starlette/middleware/body_limit.py) and max_body_size on Starlette, Router, Mount and Route. Multipart temp files now close on any exception (BaseException). Tests and docs are added. The three listed test files pass (152 passed). I did not run the rest of the suite or any lint/type checks. The sandbox only allowed `aih check` on the listed test files.

One design choice: the middleware does not check a declared Content-Length when the request starts. It checks it when the app first calls receive() or starts its response. Checking up front would make an outer app limit reject a request that an inner route or mount is configured to raise. A handler that never reads the body still gets a 413, because the check also runs when it sends its response. The cost is that the app is called before a too-large declared length is rejected. A nested middleware does reject immediately, since its limit is final.

criteria_notes.note: test_body_over_limit (413, text/plain, 'Content Too Large'); test_response_started_already_sends_no_second_response (receive returns http.disconnect, later sends dropped); test_client_disconnect_after_limit_is_swallowed; test_client_disconnect_without_limit_propagates. tests/test_body_limit.py::test_response_started_before_limit_is_not_followed_by_second_response covers the same at app level.

test_declared_content_length_is_rejected_before_body_is_read (raw receive never called); test_declared_content_length_fails_fast; test_understated_content_length_is_enforced; test_invalid_content_length_is_ignored. tests/test_body_limit.py::test_application_limit_applies_before_routing covers a declared length on a 404 path.
tests/test_body_limit.py: test_default_is_unlimited, test_application_limit, test_router_limit, test_mount_limit, test_route_limit.

tests/test_body_limit.py: test_application_limit_applies_before_routing, test_inner_limits_raise_outer_limit and test_inner_limits_lower_outer_limit (route, mount and router, with Content-Length and chunked bodies). tests/middleware/test_body_limit.py::test_nested_middleware_overrides_limit.

tests/test_body_limit.py::test_multipart_overhead_counts_toward_limit (limit one byte under the full body size gives 413) and test_multipart_temp_files_closed_when_limit_is_crossed (multi-chunk raw ASGI, temp file closed). tests/test_formparsers.py::test_multipart_closes_tempfile_on_any_interruption (RuntimeError mid-parse closes the file).
Documented in docs/middleware.md (RequestBodyLimitMiddleware section), docs/applications.md (Limiting the request body size) and docs/routing.md (Limiting the request body size). No test; docs only.
